goldens.comment: The PollFeed job calls open(SiteSetting.feed_polling_url) without validating the URL, allowing an attacker who controls the feed_polling_url site setting to make the server fetch arbitrary internal or external URLs.

postMessage targetOrigin should be the origin (scheme+host+port), not the full referrer URL; using the full URL will cause the message to be dropped and prevent resizing.

The code sets X-Frame-Options: ALLOWALL which completely disables clickjacking protection. The referer validation can be bypassed (referer headers are easily spoofed), and the fallback to empty string for nil referer masks validation failures.

The TopicEmbed.import method is susceptible to a NoMethodError if the contents parameter is nil when attempting to append a string, and an XSS vulnerability due to unescaped url interpolation in the generated HTML.
The ERB block closes with end if, which is invalid Ruby/ERB and will raise at render; it should just be end to close the if block.

Calling `i.content.scrub` assumes that `i.content` is always populated. However, many RSS feeds do not provide a `content` field, leading to a potential nil pointer exception when `i.content` is nil. A fallback to `description` should be implemented to prevent crashes.

An unescaped request header (request.referer) is interpolated into JavaScript without proper escaping, which can lead to XSS vulnerabilities if the referer contains malicious content. This issue can allow attackers to execute arbitrary scripts in the context of the application.

adjudication_records.issue_text: topic_embed.rb:13 interpolates `url` unescaped into an `<a href>` tag; a crafted URL passing the host check yields stored XSS in a `raw_html` post

adjudication.rationale: In `app/models/topic_embed.rb` the import method appends HTML to `contents` using `"#{url}"` with `url` taken from external input (RSS item link/id or remote URL). The only validation is `url =~ /^https?\:\/\//`, which does not prevent quotes or other characters that can break out of the single-quoted `href` attribute (e.g., `http://eviltrout.com/' onmouseover='alert(1)`). Because imported posts are created with `cook_method: Post.cook_methods[:raw_html]` and `Post#cook` returns `raw` unchanged for `raw_html`, this unescaped HTML is stored and later rendered (e.g., `embed/best.html.erb` uses `<%= raw post.cooked %>`), enabling stored XSS. The host check in `TopicRetriever#invalid_host?` only compares `URI(@embed_url).host` and would still pass for such a crafted URL with a valid host and malicious path/query.

adjudication_records.issue_text: poll_feed.rb:35 stores feed item HTML unescaped as `raw_html`, so any script or event handler in a third-party feed executes for every user; Readability whitelist in `import_remote` also permits `javascript:` URLs

adjudication.rationale: Yes. In `Jobs::PollFeed#poll_feed`, it takes `i.content` from the feed, runs `CGI.unescapeHTML(i.content.scrub)`, and passes it to `TopicEmbed.import`. `TopicEmbed.import` creates the post with `cook_method: Post.cook_methods[:raw_html]`, and `Post#cook` returns `raw` directly for `raw_html`, explicitly skipping the normal cooking/sanitization pipeline. The embed view then renders it with `<%= raw post.cooked %>`, so arbitrary HTML from a third-party feed (including `<script>` or inline event handlers) would be served to users and can execute in the browser (XSS). The additional claim about `import_remote` allowing `javascript:` URLs depends on the `ruby-readability` gem’s sanitization behavior and isn’t directly proven by the diff, but the core un-sanitized raw HTML issue is verifiable in the changes.

adjudication_records.issue_text: embed_controller.rb:26 gates topic creation only on the forgeable `Referer` header, allowing unauthenticated unbounded topic creation as `embed_by_username` with outbound fetches; the per-URL Redis throttle does not limit this

adjudication.rationale: The new public route `get 'embed/best' => 'embed#best'` will enqueue `Jobs::RetrieveTopic` whenever `TopicEmbed.topic_id_for_embed(embed_url)` is nil. The only access control in `EmbedController#ensure_embeddable` is `URI(request.referer||'').host == SiteSetting.embeddable_host`, but `Referer` is a client-controlled/forgeable header for non-browser clients, so an unauthenticated attacker can call `/embed/best?embed_url=http://<embeddable_host>/...` with a matching forged Referer and trigger `TopicRetriever#fetch_http`, which does `open(url).read` and then `TopicEmbed.import_remote`/`PostCreator` as the configured `embed_by_username`. The Redis throttle in `TopicRetriever#retrieved_recently?` is keyed by full URL (`retrieved:#{@embed_url}`) and only throttles repeats of the same URL for 60s; it does not prevent creating many topics by varying the URL path on the allowed host.

adjudication_records.issue_text: poll_feed.rb:29 uses `Kernel#open` on admin-controlled `feed_polling_url`, enabling shell command execution via `|` prefix or local file reads; should use `URI(...).open` or Net::HTTP
matched_golden_ids: The PollFeed job calls open(SiteSetting.feed_polling_url) without validating the URL, allowing an attacker who controls the feed_polling_url site setting to make the server fetch arbitrary internal or external URLs.
adjudication_records.primary_judge_reasoning: Both point to the same core problem: PollFeed uses Ruby `open`/`Kernel#open` on a site setting (`feed_polling_url`) without validation, letting an attacker influence what the server opens/fetches. The candidate emphasizes additional `Kernel#open` dangers (pipe command execution, local file reads), but it still includes the golden issue’s unvalidated, attacker-controlled URL leading to arbitrary server-side fetching (SSRF).

adjudication_records.issue_text: post.rb:133 lets any user who can edit a `raw_html` post submit arbitrary unsanitized HTML via the normal edit UI since `PostRevisor` preserves `cook_method`

adjudication.rationale: The diff introduces a new `cook_method` enum with a `:raw_html` mode and changes `Post#cook` to immediately `return raw` when `cook_method == Post.cook_methods[:raw_html]`, bypassing the normal cooking/rendering pipeline (which would typically sanitize/transform content). `TopicEmbed.import` explicitly creates imported posts with `cook_method: Post.cook_methods[:raw_html]`. On subsequent edits, `PostRevisor#revise!` updates `raw` but does not change/reset `cook_method`, so the post remains in `raw_html` mode and future edits will continue to be served as raw, unsanitized HTML. Thus, anyone able to edit such a post can inject arbitrary HTML that will be rendered directly.

adjudication_records.issue_text: embed_controller.rb:26 requiring a `Referer` breaks legitimate embeds when browsers strip it (HTTPS→HTTP navigation, `Referrer-Policy: no-referrer`), causing 403

adjudication.rationale: In EmbedController#ensure_embeddable, access is denied unless `URI(request.referer || '').host == SiteSetting.embeddable_host`. This means requests with a missing/stripped Referer header will always raise `Discourse::InvalidAccess` (e.g., if the embedding page sets `Referrer-Policy: no-referrer` or when navigating/embedding from HTTPS to an HTTP Discourse instance under the common default `no-referrer-when-downgrade` policy). That would break otherwise legitimate embeds because the controller requires a Referer to authorize the request.

adjudication_records.issue_text: poll_feed.rb:31 has no per-item error handling, so one bad item (nil title, bad URI in `absolutize_urls`, RecordNotUnique) aborts import of all remaining items

adjudication.rationale: In app/jobs/scheduled/poll_feed.rb, rss.items.each iterates and processes each item without any per-item rescue. Several calls inside the loop can raise and would stop the entire job, preventing remaining items from importing: e.g., i.content.scrub will raise NoMethodError if i.content is nil; open(SiteSetting.feed_polling_url) / SimpleRSS.parse can raise; and TopicEmbed.import can raise via TopicEmbed.create! (unique index on embed_url makes RecordNotUnique possible under concurrency or duplicate URLs). Since exceptions aren’t handled per item, a single bad item can abort the rest of the import.

adjudication_records.issue_text: topic_embed.rb:64 protocol-relative URLs (`//cdn.example.com/x.png`) match `start_with?('/')` and are incorrectly rewritten to `http://host/cdn.example.com/x.png`

adjudication.rationale: Yes. In `TopicEmbed.absolutize_urls`, both `` href and `` src are rewritten when `start_with?('/')` is true. Protocol-relative URLs like `//cdn.example.com/x.png` also satisfy `start_with?('/')`, and the code does `href.sub(/^\/+/, '')`, turning `//cdn.example.com/x.png` into `cdn.example.com/x.png`, then prefixes it with `#{prefix}/`, yielding `http:///cdn.example.com/x.png` (or https), which is incorrect. This is directly verifiable from the diff logic.

adjudication_records.issue_text: topic_embed.rb:21 race condition: concurrent imports of the same URL both pass `exists?`, loser hits unique index in `TopicEmbed.create!`, rolling back topic/post but not PostCreator's enqueued jobs, and the exception is unhandled

adjudication.rationale: In `TopicEmbed.import`, the code does a read-then-create sequence: `embed = TopicEmbed.where(embed_url: url).first` and if blank it enters a transaction and eventually calls `TopicEmbed.create!` on a table with a unique index on `embed_url` (migration adds `add_index :topic_embeds, :embed_url, unique: true`). Two concurrent imports of the same URL can both observe `embed.blank?` and both create a post/topic, then the second will raise a uniqueness violation (`RecordNotUnique`) at `create!`. There is no rescue, so the exception will bubble up (e.g., from feed polling / retrieval). The extra claim about PostCreator-enqueued jobs not rolling back is not verifiable from this diff, but the race + unhandled uniqueness exception is a real defect introduced/left by this implementation.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Migrations create_top_topics.rb:3 and create_topic_embeds.rb:3 use `force: true`, silently dropping existing tables and data; editing already-shipped migrations is a red flag

adjudication.rationale: The diff changes an existing migration `db/migrate/20131223171005_create_top_topics.rb` to `create_table :top_topics, force: true`, which will drop the table if it already exists when the migration is run (e.g., on a fresh setup with a pre-existing table, or if the migration is rolled back and re-run). Additionally, the new migration `db/migrate/20131217174004_create_topic_embeds.rb` uses `create_table :topic_embeds, force: true`, which also instructs Rails to drop any existing `topic_embeds` table. Using `force: true` in migrations is a real footgun because it can silently destroy data, and editing an already-present migration to add this behavior is a legitimate red flag.

adjudication_records.issue_text: topic_embed.rb:79 lookup is an exact string match on `embed_url`, so query params, trailing slashes, and fragments create separate topics for the same article

adjudication.rationale: In `TopicEmbed`, both lookup and uniqueness are based on the raw `embed_url` string: `TopicEmbed.where(embed_url: url).first` in `.import` and `TopicEmbed.where(embed_url: embed_url).pluck(:topic_id).first` in `.topic_id_for_embed`. The migration also adds a unique index on `embed_url` with no normalization. Since no canonicalization is performed (e.g., stripping fragments, normalizing trailing slashes, sorting/removing query params), different URL representations of the same article will be treated as distinct and can create separate `topic_embeds`/topics.

adjudication_records.issue_text: topic_retriever.rb:41 every miss for a new URL synchronously runs a full RSS fetch-and-import of the entire feed, which is attacker-triggerable

adjudication.rationale: Yes. In lib/topic_retriever.rb `perform_retrieve` unconditionally runs `Jobs::PollFeed.new.execute({})` whenever `SiteSetting.feed_polling_enabled?` is true and the requested `@embed_url` is not already present in `TopicEmbed` (a “miss”). `Jobs::PollFeed#poll_feed` then does `SimpleRSS.parse open(SiteSetting.feed_polling_url)` and iterates `rss.items.each`, importing every item in the feed. This happens inline within the `RetrieveTopic` job (not deferred to a separate scheduled poll), and the only throttle in `retrieved_recently?` is per-embed_url (redis key includes the full URL), so an attacker can bypass it by requesting many distinct `embed_url` values under the allowed host (and referer can be forged in direct requests), repeatedly triggering full feed fetch+parse+import work.

adjudication_records.issue_text: topic_embed.rb:59 port logic should compare against `uri.default_port`; `https://host:80` and `http://host:443` produce wrong prefixes

adjudication.rationale: In TopicEmbed.absolutize_urls, the prefix is built as `scheme://host` and then the port is appended only if `uri.port != 80 && uri.port != 443`. This treats both 80 and 443 as “default” for all schemes. For URLs like `https://example.com:80/...` or `http://example.com:443/...`, `uri.port` equals 80/443 so the code will *not* append the explicit port, producing an incorrect prefix (`https://example.com` or `http://example.com`) and therefore incorrect absolutized links/images. Comparing against `uri.default_port` (scheme-aware) would avoid this.

adjudication_records.issue_text: post.rb:133 `cook(*args)` ignores the passed raw and returns `self.raw`, so callers passing a different string silently get wrong content

adjudication.rationale: The diff adds an early return in `Post#cook(*args)` when `cook_method` is `:raw_html`, returning `self.raw` and skipping the normal cooking pipeline. While this does ignore any `*args`, the diff does not show that `cook` is meant to accept a raw string argument or that any caller passes alternate content to `cook` expecting it to be used. In the shown new usage (`TopicEmbed.import`), the intent is explicitly to treat the post’s stored `raw` as already-cooked HTML, so returning `raw` is consistent. The proposed finding assumes a calling convention (“passed raw”) that is not verifiable from the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: topic_embed.rb:13 `contents << ...` mutates the caller's string and raises on frozen strings

adjudication.rationale: In `TopicEmbed.import(user, url, title, contents)`, the line `contents << "\n<hr>..."` appends in-place to the `contents` string object passed by the caller. That creates a real, observable side effect (the caller’s string is modified after the call) and will also raise `FrozenError` if the caller supplies a frozen string (e.g., a frozen constant, or under `frozen_string_literal: true`). The mutation is directly verifiable from the diff and isn’t guarded against (no `dup`/rebind).

adjudication_records.issue_text: disqus.thor:148 import now depends on a live HTTP fetch of every thread link, so any 404/timeout aborts the whole import

adjudication.rationale: In `lib/tasks/disqus.thor`, the import path changed from creating a topic using the thread’s provided metadata (`PostCreator.new(... raw: "[Permalink](...)" ...)`) to `TopicEmbed.import_remote(user, t[:link], title: t[:title])`. `TopicEmbed.import_remote` does a live `open(url).read` (via `open-uri`) with no error handling. If any thread link returns 404, times out, or otherwise raises an exception, it will bubble up and terminate the Thor task, aborting the rest of the import loop. This new dependency on successful HTTP fetches is directly introduced by the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: disqus.thor `--category` option was removed without replacement

adjudication.rationale: The diff clearly removes the Thor option `method_option :category` and all logic that used it to look up a `category_id` and pass it to `PostCreator`. However, this is a behavioral/CLI change (the import task no longer supports choosing a category) rather than a verifiable defect: the updated code now imports via `TopicEmbed.import_remote(...)` and no longer uses `PostCreator` directly, so there is no internal inconsistency or runtime error introduced by the removal shown in the diff. Whether a replacement is needed is a product/compatibility concern not provable as a bug from this diff alone.

adjudication_records.issue_text: embed.js:7 `discourseUrl + "embed/best"` assumes a trailing slash on `discourseUrl`, producing `hostembed/best` without it

adjudication.rationale: In app/assets/javascripts/embed.js the iframe URL is built via string concatenation: `iframe.src = discourseUrl + "embed/best?embed_url=" + ...`. If `discourseUrl` is provided as `https://forum.example.com` (no trailing `/`), the resulting path becomes `https://forum.example.comembed/best?...`, which is an invalid URL. The code introduces no normalization (e.g., ensuring a trailing slash) to prevent this.

adjudication_records.issue_text: poll_feed_spec.rb:12 the three 'requires X' tests rely on other settings defaulting to false/blank and pass regardless of which condition is checked

adjudication.rationale: Yes. `Jobs::PollFeed#execute` only calls `poll_feed` when **all three** conditions are true (`feed_polling_enabled?` && `feed_polling_url.present?` && `embed_by_username.present?`). In `spec/jobs/poll_feed_spec.rb`, each “requires X” example stubs only one setting (e.g., `feed_polling_enabled?` to false) but does not stub the other two to truthy values. Given the defaults added in `config/site_settings.yml` (`feed_polling_enabled: false`, `feed_polling_url: ''`, `embed_by_username: ''`), the condition will be false regardless, so those tests can pass even if the specific requirement being tested were removed or broken. This is a real, verifiable test deficiency introduced in the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: No test coverage for `poll_feed`, `perform_retrieve`, the Redis throttle, `import_remote`, or `absolutize_urls` edge cases (protocol-relative URLs, ports, bad URIs)

adjudication.rationale: The diff adds new behavior in Jobs::PollFeed#poll_feed, TopicRetriever#perform_retrieve/#retrieved_recently? (Redis setnx/expire throttle), and TopicEmbed.import_remote/absolutize_urls. The added specs only cover PollFeed#execute guard conditions, and TopicRetriever#retrieve behavior while stubbing retrieved_recently? (so the Redis throttle implementation and perform_retrieve internals aren’t exercised). TopicEmbed specs cover one basic absolutize_urls case (leading “/” for href/src) but not protocol-relative URLs, ports, or invalid URI inputs, and there is no spec for import_remote. Therefore the claim of missing coverage for these areas is verifiable from the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: poll_feed.rb:20 `feed_key` is defined but never used

adjudication.rationale: In `app/jobs/scheduled/poll_feed.rb`, the instance method `feed_key` (around line 20) is defined and memoizes a Redis key, but there are no references to `feed_key` anywhere else in the diff (including within `poll_feed`/`execute`). Nothing in the shown code path calls it, so it is dead/unused code as introduced.

adjudication_records.issue_text: retrieve_topic.rb `require_dependency 'email/sender'` is unused

adjudication.rationale: In `app/jobs/regular/retrieve_topic.rb`, the diff adds `require_dependency 'email/sender'` but the job implementation never references `Email::Sender` (or anything from `email/sender`). The only explicit dependency used is `TopicRetriever` (required on the next line) plus `User`/`Discourse` constants that come from the Rails app. This makes the `email/sender` require redundant/unneeded as written.
